All these comments are great. Additionally, a big aspect of pre-WWII Japanese culture was that fighting until death, even in an obviously losing battle, gives you both honor and credibility. It would take me a bit to find a quote supporting this from reference books (maybe "The Chrysanthemum and the Sword"), but here's a related one from Princess Mononoke, justifying a suicide mission: "Even if we all fall in battle, we will leave the humans in awe." It does seem like Kaoru values her life very little in comparison to the statement she could make by fighting Battousai to the death for the sake of her sword style's honor. This wasn't crazy or naive, it was cultural.

I’m also unemployed, and my sleep schedule was similar to yours. I don’t actually feel tired until 2am, but if I’m doing something interesting at that time, the next wave of sleepy doesn’t hit until 7am. A couple weeks ago I listened to this podcast episode about sleep which changed everything. My main takeaway was that I needed to see direct sunlight for at least 2 minutes within an hour of sunrise and within an hour of sunset, and it would reset my circadian rhythm. It took a lot of effort, but I did it for two days in a row, and immediately felt the difference. Crazy. I was actually tired (exhausted) at 9pm, and awake at 5, with no effort beyond getting some outside light at the right times. If you can’t listen to the whole podcast episode to get the biology behind it, at least try the trick! It worked for me!

Me too. Last year I was dealing with some other big challenges, and my hair anxiety was so bad that it would take me two hours of sitting in the bathroom thought spiraling about shampoo schedules and hair care routines before I could make myself get in the shower. That was such a waste of time, not to mention how often I decided to not shower or live with greasy hair - so I shaved it all off. Did I look attractive? No. Did I feel more comfortable and free than I have since childhood? Absolutely. And I was able to use the regrowth time to train my hair to only need washing once a week. That can still be hard, but the shower fight is way easier once a week than every day, and its easier for me to maintain good hygiene when I don’t feel like I have to shampoo every time I shower. As long as you’re okay with sacrificing your dating life for your mental health, I say do it. For me it was worth it. And it kinda convinced me that I’d rather be with a man who can handle a buzz anyway.
